style: 3D cartoon, Pixar, dry deadpan satire, vertical 9:16 frame, taller than wide
motion_rule: the world flies at him every beat: mice, walnuts and coins launch across frame and hit the glass, ONE of them a wing from the lens in every beat; he never freezes, his wings, head and talons drive across frame each beat; the camera swings past him to a new shot size each beat; ONE sideways move per beat, never chained; his face never under a third of frame, beak visible; everything crosses the frame or comes at the lens, never up or down the frame
character: a huge tawny eagle-owl with ear tufts and orange eyes, perched on a beam and working his wings, face and beak clear
second_characters: A SWARM of mice in grey coats pouring out of the bins with his coins, ONE of them a wing from the lens every beat, crossing frame and hitting the glass; all of them moving
props: A SWARM of walnuts and coins stuffed into every crack of the loft; ONE clay money jar, out of sight until 6.90
prop_continuity: walnuts and coins leave the cracks from 0.00, the jar exists only from 6.90
environment: a sunlit grain loft packed wall to wall with bins and stuffed cracks a wing away, boards and beams raking the lens, mice streaming everywhere, a lit yard through the open gable
light_events: white noon through the boards, shafts sweeping his face every beat, a hard rim on his tufts

audio.delivery: a level male chest voice around 130 Hz, unhurried, laying each word down, even 4 syllables per second, beats filled edge to edge
audio.pronunciation: na-ko-PLE-ni-ya, kog-DA, za-BYL, ot-lo-ZHIL, I-na-che, E-to, ot-LO-zhen-ny, ras-HOD
audio.pacing: speech fills 0.00-1.25, 1.55-3.85 and 4.15-6.90, first word at 0.00; after 6.90 not a word, wings, coins and squeaks fill the track to 10.00
audio.lip_sync: his beak opens on every syllable, no voice over
audio.sfx: wings beating, coins spilling, mice squeaking, boards creaking, walnuts knocking

timeline.a: his face already fills the glass, head screwed fully backwards at us, ONE mouse crossing the lens with his coin
he snaps his beak and a walnut flies off the beam across the lens
he flares one wing across frame, the camera swinging wide past him, mice pouring out of the bins
he drives his face at the lens, a walnut hurled past his ear by a mouse
he screws his head round the other way, the loft swinging past behind him
he rips a walnut out of a crack and hurls it past the lens, coins spilling after it
he beats both wings and the whole swarm of mice launches at the glass with his coins
a mouse in a grey coat slaps the empty jar into his talons and he hurls it at the lens, his face filling the glass
he drives his beak into the glass, feathers and coins whipping past
he throws both wings wide across frame as the bins empty past the lens, the last mouse crossing with a coin

must_appear: at 0.00 his face already fills the glass with his head screwed fully backwards and a mouse already crossing the lens; a mouse or a coin crosses the lens in every beat; nothing touches him before 6.90; the jar is put into his talons at 6.90 and he throws it at the lens; every word spoken, the last by 6.90; his beak opens on every syllable
negative_prompt: subtitles, watermark, letterbox, horizontal frame, night, dark scene, a static camera, a still background, a parked hero, a hero moving up or down the frame, a wide or distant hero, standing bystanders, slow motion, letters, digits, a word not in the lines, a closed beak while speaking, anything touching him before 6.90, a third wing on him, multiple owls, a foreign accent
